g.text: B · ANS operator — the reference implementation
all three daemons serve Swagger UI at /docs
ANS never writes DNS or serves challenge files
on the owner’s behalf. The RA relays the CA’s
challenges and verifies what the owner publishes.
is a port interface in internal/port/ (swappable)
SQLite store · file-based ECDSA P-256 key manager
server-cert issuer: self-signed CA or an ACME CA
DNS verifier: noop | lookup · HTTP-01 verifier
producer-key trust store (which RA keys may ingest)
ES256 JWS → leaf = SHA-256(0x00 ‖ event) → logId
every result carries the agent’s TL receipt URI
clients verify against the TL, not the finder
The finder never talks to the TL: it hands clients the TL URLs they need to check its results.
then verifies the result against the TL ⑦
end-to-end lifecycle on a local stack
① Owner registers: POST /v2/ans/agents with identity + server CSRs (authenticated)
② RA relays the CA’s domain-control challenges; owner publishes DNS-01 TXT / HTTP-01
③ verify-acme issues the certs; verify-dns checks _ans / _ans-badge / SVCB / TLSA → ACTIVE
④ RA → TL: signed event (X-Signature = detached ES256 JWS). Activation is sealed before the RA
reports success; revocation and other lifecycle events ride the outbox worker. TL returns a logId.
⑤ Finder polls GET /v1/agents/events (TL-acknowledged rows only) into its FTS5 catalog
⑥ Client → Finder: POST /v1/search; every result carries the agent’s TL receipt URI
⑦ Verifier → TL: /root-keys, receipt, badge, checkpoint, tiles → proof checked offline
⑧ Optional: _ans-badge.<fqdn> TXT lookup resolves an agent name to its agentId
